title: What Stayed
subtitle: Regret is not always a teachable parable
sourceCredit: This American Life, Episode 541, “Regrets, I’ve Had a Few”

shot.title: Three unrelated objects
shot.direction: Separate panels contain a broom, an arm, and a shoe. They belong to separate accounts.
shot.soundDirection: Three motif sounds: broom scrape, quiet clinic ambience, shoe on pavement.

illustration.direction: CHILD ONLY, first unrelated account. A curly-haired girl in brick-red cardigan stands in a quiet domestic hallway beside a broom leaning against the wall. Her hands hold each other uneasily and she glances toward someone entirely offscreen. The broom casts one long ordinary shadow. No tattooed adult or walker appears.

companions.direction: ADULT ONLY, second unrelated account. A stocky shaved-headed bearded man in a grey rolled-sleeve shirt sits at a quiet clinic appointment table, turning his own forearm upward and looking at it with sober responsibility. The old marking is covered by a plain gauze area or indistinct neutral patch; no hateful emblem, readable tattoo, blood or child from the first account.

WALKER ONLY, third unrelated account. Slender straight-brown-haired man in olive coat sits on a park bench, one shoe removed and supported in his hands as he feels along its interior lining. His socked foot rests safely on the ground; the other shoe stays on. No tattoo, clinic, broom or child; small physical irritation at its own scale.
